located_proof_sources.quote: ROOT ORIGINAL feasibility calculation for a DIFFERENT FULL uniform inference question: write W_lambda(x)=prod lambda_i^x_i/x_i!, F=-logW. For complete binary lengthL, choose integer A>=2+L+d+sum lambda_i+sum x0_i+ceil(log(100d/epsilon)), computable with rational rounding. Then F(x0)<=2A^2 (enlarging fixed numerical constants), sum lambda_i<=A, and for U=100A^3 the unrestricted Poisson Chernoff bound gives sum_{max x_i>=U} W_lambda(x)/W_lambda(x0) <=d*exp(A+2A^2)*(eA/U)^U<epsilon/100. Since Z_Gamma>=W_lambda(x0), this is a valid absolute-tail-to-CONDITIONAL-mass bound even for exponentially rare classes, with O(L) bits to encode U. Truncating the cube does NOT replace original reachability by connectivity inside the cube. Separately, positive-real log-Gamma remainder after orderr is <=|B_2r|/[2r(2r-1)t^(2r-1)]; using |B_2r|<=4(2r)!/(2pi)^(2r), t>=8r gives geometric-in-r error. This supplies an actual accuracy-bit opening beyond072's 1/n approximation; it does not yet supply the complete uniform support/compiler/mixture proof. For any weakly reversible structure and positive rational lambda, choose positive rational cycle-circulation q_r on its complex graph and kappa_r=q_r/lambda^y_r; complex balance atlambda follows. Thus the new conditioned-Poisson question includes genuinely nonconservative complex-balanced equilibria, rather than claiming arbitrary original non-balanced rates have that law.
